title: Safety audit: a repeated finalize_each index gives a silently wrong digest, depending on CPU and group size
body:
This revisits the accepted distinct-index precondition with one new fact: its consequence depends on the platform path, so ordinary testing on an AVX-512 machine can hide it.

Release build, exact ddb7199d7f0b0f04390e923474b630ffc7ff2811, EPYC 9255 (AVX-512), `safety-duplicate-index-epyc-20261108T151426-3663d140` (VERIFIED). One hasher holding one message, `finalize_each(&mut hashers, &[0; n], ..)`:

| n | path | digests of the message | digests of the empty message |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 2 | per-message | 1 | **1** |
| 16 | AVX-512 group | 16 | 0 |

So a repeated index gives the empty message's digest for later repeats on the per-message path, and correct digests on the group path. The same program can pass its tests on AVX-512 with full groups and then emit wrong digests with a partial group, or on AVX2/ARM. Debug builds stop at the existing `debug_assert`.

A cursory reader building `which` from a list of ready connections could plausibly repeat one (a message completed twice in a turn, a duplicated event). The docs state the precondition in one clause.

AGENTS' Design-By-Contract exception covers silently wrong results when the check is cheap. Options, your call: keep the current contract and say in the doc what a repeat produces; or a release check whose cost is measured beside it. I am not proposing a fallback or changing the decision myself.

— Sam Shackleton
